requirements.title: Relational intrinsic operations cover numeric, character, enumeration, and enum operand families
requirements.definition: The relational intrinsic operators are .EQ., .NE., .GT., .GE., .LT., .LE., ==, /=, >, >=, <, and <=. A relational intrinsic operation uses one of those operators. Numeric relational operations have numeric operands; character relational operations have character operands whose kind type parameters shall be the same; enumeration relational operations have operands of the same enumeration type; enum relational operations have one enum operand and the other operand of the same enum type or an integer expression involving an enumerator of that type. Table 10.2 gives logical results and the admitted equality and ordering families.

review_rationale: Independent source review in doc/source_audits/batch_100.json reads all27 original base units and81 fine units of 10.1.3,10.1.4 and10.1.5.1 in full, together with the cited 7.x,10.1.6 through10.1.12 and15.4.3.4.x material and the registered 10.1.2 grammar catalogues, and independently enumerates the evaluation freedoms in scope before comparing them with the candidate. This scope is where the processor latitude lives, so a permission wrongly promoted to a requirement, or a plan that infers behaviour from evaluation order, would corrupt every later expression fixture. The review confirms that the IF, WHERE and FORALL side-effect permission and the permission for pure elemental operations to be performed in any order or simultaneously are both dispositioned as permissions rather than requirements; that the conditional skipped-evaluation effect carries no side-effect oracle; and that the freedoms owned by 10.1.7,10.1.8 and10.1.6.3 are recorded as oracle boundaries and dependencies rather than as locally owned requirements. Table10.2 is substantively correct, with the enumeration-type and character-kind distinctions preserved. No plan infers anything from which operand was evaluated or in what order, asserts a result that a mathematically equivalent rewrite could change, or relies on a floating-point tolerance, and grouping of an associative intrinsic operation is not claimed to be value-observable. The expression grammar remains owned by the registered 10.1.2 catalogues and intrinsic assignment by 10.2.1.3. All facets remain pending source plans; no case, execution, oracle or fixture approval is created.
